title: 32nd sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with routine business: minutes of sittings 25 to 28 were accepted, two Judiciary Committee seats were refilled, and a committee deadline was announced. Members then debated Economic, Social, Judiciary and Joint committee reports on seven bills, with the health services bill drawing the longest and most partisan exchange about past and present handling of Aasandha and hospitals. After a break the Majlis voted on all seven bills and passed them, five unanimously (77-0) and the built-environment and decentralisation bills 67-10. The chair closed by reporting that 82.9% of matters submitted to the Majlis were complete and that the last sitting of the session would be that night at 9:00 pm. Part of the opening attendance figures is garbled in the text. This part of the minutes contains only the electronic voting records, with no debate text. Members voted on four bills, with 80 members present and 79 eligible to vote (the Speaker does not vote). Two amendment bills passed unanimously among those voting, and two passed 67 to 10.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee reports on the business registration and financial securities bills.
Said the securities amendments align the law with the new foreign investment law, after consulting government bodies.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the business registration bill, saying registration shows how many firms operate and eases economic planning.
Called false reports on state finances irresponsible and urged setting clear rules for spending state money.
Urged faster court processes and said she would later propose adding 'Sharia and law' to who may practise as a lawyer.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said many firms were registered but contractors went unpaid, and criticised the previous government's contracts.
Wanted competitive markets for small firms, not registration alone; hoped the changes open opportunities for them.
Said health reform needs a master plan prioritising doctors and services over new hospital buildings.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the health picture is unclear and raised IGM Hospital equipment shortages and Aasandha access problems.
Spoke after the chair cited the rule against disrupting a member; again stressed patient access concerns.
Backed the Legal Profession amendments, noting the Attorney General's removal from the Bar Council committee and simpler document certification.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Presented the Joint Committee report on the built environment bill, passed in committee after four meetings and consultations.
Said committee members from all parties raised no concern about council powers, and councils would keep land decisions.
Presented the Decentralised Administration Act amendment report, passed in committee after consulting the housing ministry.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Backed the business registration report but flagged a remaining provision on land held by firms whose shares pass to foreigners.
Argued the built environment bill weakens atoll and city councils and urged revision after consulting councillors.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Presented the Judiciary Committee report: lawyers alone would run the Bar Council committee and schools could certify true copies.
Said the main aim is to keep government influence out of lawyers' affairs.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Said the bills bring Maldivian law in line with signed international agreements and urged passing them as the committee approved.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Urged passing the amendments quickly for the nation's sake and called for responsible talk about state finances.

speakers.name: Asma Rasheed
positions: Presented the Social Committee report: amendments make preventive care part of the health system and set standards for it.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the report and said Aasandha and NSPA arrears and unpaid foreign debts were left by the previous administration.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill as strengthening the system and using state funds better; criticised past handling of health assets.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Welcomed the bill's preventive-care focus and criticised the previous government's medicine import arrangements.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the amendments suit the economic situation and criticised MDP-era health promises, such as the Velidhoo health centre.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said Aasandha arrears of about MVR 1.1 billion hurt hospitals, and raised ambulance and service gaps in Fuvahmulah.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Cited rising NSPA arrears (MVR 491 million to about 1.5 billion) and asked the government to publish reserve figures.

speakers.name: Ahmed Siyam Mohamed
positions: Said the health sector had failed for over thirty years and Aasandha had not helped; supported rebuilding from the ground up.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 25 to 28 of 2024 accepted without amendments.
Judiciary Committee seats refilled: Milandhoo and Thulusdhoo members replace the Hulhudhoo and Faresmaathodaa members.
Committee deadline of 10 October 2024 announced for the Urban Development Bill.

Maldives Financial Securities Act (2/2006) amendment bill passed 77-0.

Legal Profession Act (5/2019) amendment bill passed 77-0.
Built Environment Planning and Management Bill passed 67-10.
Decentralised Administration Act (7/2010) amendment bill passed 67-10.
